Taling Ngam is the long, quiet village beach on Samui's south-west coast, 11 km (15–20 minutes) south of Nathon and 29 km (40–50 minutes) from Chaweng. It has fishing boats on the sand, luxury resorts on the cliffs behind and, on clear evenings, Samui's best sunset, with the sun dropping behind the Five Islands (Koh Si Koh Ha). The water is shallow and tidal, and calm for much of the year. It is also home to Baan Suan Lung Khai, Samui's MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2026 southern seafood restaurant (reservation required).

Map of Taling Ngam

Taling Ngam lies between Lipa Noi to the north and Thong Krut to the south. The ring road runs inland here; Route 4170 and smaller lanes drop to the coast. The beach faces west across the bay, with the Five Islands offshore to the south-west.

The beach and tides

Taling Ngam is a long, gently curving stretch of sand with longtail fishing boats pulled up in front of the village, coconut palms and a few beachfront restaurants and small resorts. The big luxury resorts sit on the cliffs and hills behind, with their own beach clubs. The sea is shallow and tidal. At high tide the water comes up to the palm line and is good for a swim or a paddle; at low tide it retreats over wide flats that are fun for children to explore and good for photos at sunset. Check the tide before you plan a swim:

[kp_tide_now]

Swimming and safety

  • Calm most of the year: the west coast is sheltered from the October–December north-east monsoon waves that close Chaweng and Lamai, so Taling Ngam is often flat when the east coast has red flags. Heavy rain still falls; November is the wettest month at about 445 mm.
  • Shallow: good for families at mid to high tide; at low tide you may wade a long way for knee-deep water.
  • Underfoot: mostly sand, with some rock and shell patches; water shoes help near the boats.
  • Box jellyfish: present in Samui waters, with risk higher in calm, hot weather after rain and in the monsoon months. Avoid swimming at dusk; vinegar for at least 30 seconds on a sting, no rubbing, call 1669.
  • Boats: keep clear of longtails coming in and out of the shore.
  • Medical help: Koh Samui Hospital (government) is in Nathon, about 20 minutes north (+66 77 913 200); the private hospitals are in the Chaweng area, 40–50 minutes away.

See Koh Samui beach safety.

The Five Islands and the sunset

The Five Islands, Koh Si Koh Ha ("four islands, five islands"), are a cluster of small, steep islets off the south-west coast. From any one viewpoint you can only see four of them, because one hides behind another, hence the name. Swiftlets nest in their cliffs, and the nests are collected for the Chinese bird's-nest trade. They are a landmark rather than a beach stop: you see them from the shore or from a boat. On clear evenings the sun sets behind and beside the islets, which is why many locals rate Taling Ngam as Samui's best sunset. Approximate mid-month sunset times:

MonthsSunsetSky
November–December17:55–18:00Often cloudy; monsoon rain
January18:15Clearing
February–May18:30Clearest, driest months
June–August18:40–18:45Good; some haze and storms
September–October18:05–18:20Mixed

Arrive 30–45 minutes early and stand at the water's edge at low tide for reflections on the wet sand. Compare other spots on Koh Samui sunset spots, or watch it from the water on our Pig Island sunset tour.

Baan Suan Lung Khai and local food

Baan Suan Lung Khai, at 18/18 Moo 4, Taling Ngam, is one of only two Koh Samui restaurants in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026 Bib Gourmand list. It serves southern Thai fish and seafood dishes, with blue crab and grilled prawns among the specialities, at a moderate price level. It opens daily 11:00–14:00 and 16:30–19:00, and a reservation is required: call +66 81 416 2244, ideally a day or more ahead in high season. Its early closing time means you eat before sunset, then walk down to the beach.

Elsewhere, the village has simple Thai restaurants and beachfront places serving fresh fish, and Island View serves Thai fusion food by the beach. For seafood by the kilo, Thong Krut is 10–15 minutes south. See Koh Samui seafood and Koh Samui restaurants.

Sunset bars and nightlife

Taling Ngam has no nightlife in the party sense. Evenings revolve around the sunset, then dinner. The clifftop resorts have open-air bars with wide views over the bay, such as the Air Bar at the InterContinental (listed 17:00–22:00) and Jahn at the Conrad; check with each resort whether outside guests need a booking. After about 20:00 the village is quiet and dark. For bars and clubs you need to drive 40–50 minutes to Chaweng or 25–30 minutes to Lamai.

Chinese Temple of Guanyin

About 5 km south, towards Thong Krut, stands the Chinese Temple of Guanyin (9.4212, 99.9479), a shrine to the Buddhist goddess of mercy, open in daylight. It reflects the island's Hainanese Chinese heritage and is a short stop on the way to the Pig Island boats. Dress respectfully. More on Koh Samui temples.

Where to stay in Taling Ngam

Taling Ngam is the luxury end of the west coast. The headlands are home to large resorts with cliff-edge pool villas, including the Conrad Koh Samui (from about US$400 a night), the InterContinental Koh Samui Resort, and Nivata Koh Samui (Tapestry Collection by Hilton), plus private pool villas for rent. A few smaller beachfront resorts and guesthouses sit near the village. West-coast rooms range from about 1,500 THB for a simple room to 6,000 THB and far more for villas. It suits honeymooners and anyone after quiet sunsets, but every meal outside your resort is a drive, and the airport is 45–55 minutes away. See where to stay on Koh Samui, villas and honeymoon ideas.

The roads: Route 4170

Route 4170 is the connector between Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam and the south coast. It is steep and narrow, with blind bends, and slippery when wet. Some of the resort access roads are steeper still. In October–December, heavy rain can flood low-lying stretches in the south-west. If you are not an experienced rider, don't take a scooter up the resort hills; use a car or our transfer. Helmets are compulsory for rider and passenger, with fines up to 2,000 THB per person. See Koh Samui roads and motorbike rental.

An afternoon on the sunset coast

Because Baan Suan Lung Khai closes its evening service at 19:00, the best Taling Ngam afternoon is built backwards from the sunset. A plan for a clear day:

  1. 14:00 Drive down from Nathon (15–20 minutes) or round from Lamai (25–30 minutes) via Route 4170, in daylight.
  2. 14:30 Stop at the Chinese Temple of Guanyin on the way, or look at the boats at Thong Krut pier.
  3. 16:30 Early dinner at Baan Suan Lung Khai as the evening service opens (booked in advance).
  4. 17:45 Walk down to Taling Ngam beach; if the tide is low, stand at the edge of the wet sand for reflections.
  5. Sunset (17:55–18:45 by season) Watch the sun drop beside the Five Islands.
  6. After dark Drive back slowly; Route 4170 has blind bends and no lighting in places.

Grab coverage on the west coast is weak, especially after dark: book your return before sunset. Parking is free along the beach lanes; don't block fishermen's access to the boats. Nearby places

  • Thong Krut, 10–15 minutes south: the pier for Pig Island and Koh Tan.
  • Lipa Noi, about 10 minutes north: the shallow toddler beach and the Raja ferry pier.
  • Nathon, 15–20 minutes north: ferries, the night market and the government hospital.
  • Laem Sor Pagoda: the gold-tiled chedi on the south coast.
  • Koh Tan: the best shallow snorkelling near Samui, by boat from Thong Krut.
